action: As the university's notice urges, as reported by Daily SECU: change the passwords of the Hyangrim-tong system and other campus accounts, change any external-site password that was the same, and be wary of smishing and voice phishing impersonating universities, public agencies or financial institutions.
date_note: Day the university's Information and Computing Center issued its apology and notice, per Daily SECU (published 25 November KST); the intrusion date is not stated.
exec: A Korean national university says some users' personal data appears to have leaked from a legacy system; the scale is not disclosed.
geo_basis: country (article does not state the campus city)
plain: Suncheon National University says it found signs that some users' personal data leaked from its old Hyangrim-tong system. It has set up a page where users can check whether they were affected.
summary: Daily SECU reports that Suncheon National University's Information and Computing Center said on 24 November it detected abnormal external access attempts on its legacy Hyangrim-tong system and found signs that some users' personal data leaked. The notice says the vulnerability was patched and external access blocked, and that the incident was reported to the Personal Information Protection Commission and KISA. The article says the scale, data types and attacker are not disclosed.
title: Suncheon National University says personal data of some users appears to have leaked from legacy Hyangrim-tong system

validation.note: Single publisher (Daily SECU) relaying the university's own notice; the notice page itself was not read.

review.note: Compared date, notice contents, patch, PIPC and KISA report, undisclosed scale and user advice against Daily SECU
